_: tools/NO_SECRETS.py check D -- no tracked binaries outside an allowlist.
Six of the seven are behaviour the pre-D build did not have: it tracked
fifteen PNGs, nine of them pictures of the health record, and reported
clean every time. Against the reconstructed build each of the six fails.
Assertion 05 is the one a version control cannot prove. It says an
allowlisted icon is NOT refused -- and the pre-D build did not refuse it
either, because it refused nothing. An allowlist that is never shown to
let anything through is decoration, and the pressure on a check that
blocks a needed file is to switch the check off. So it is controlled by
mutation `emptyallow`, which empties BINARY_ALLOW: the two PWA icons are
then refused and the assertion catches it.
Assertion 02 is the owner's stated requirement in as direct a form as it
can be put: a PNG is created in a throwaway git repository, added, and
NO_SECRETS is run against that tree. Nothing is simulated and the real

assertions.name: 01 the allowlist is the two icons and every entry states its reason
02 adding any new tracked PNG fails the check, by name
03 binary content under a text extension is caught too
04 a tracked archive is refused on the same footing as an image
05 an allowlisted binary is not refused

mutation.why: empty BINARY_ALLOW so the two PWA icons are refused, and see the assertion catch an allowlist that lets nothing through
mutation.find:
BINARY_ALLOW = {
    "gutlog/icon-192.png":
        "PWA manifest icon, served by gutlog/pwa.py - an abstract glyph, no "
        "content, and the app will not install without it",
    "gutlog/icon-512.png":
        "the same icon at 512px, same manifest, same reason",
}

assertions.name: 06 with git unreachable the binary check refuses rather than passing
07 the real tree carries no tracked binary outside the allowlist
